title: How to kickstart and scale a marketplace: playbook from 17 marketplaces
summary: Lenny distills interviews with founders and early growth leads at 17 major marketplaces into a four-step playbook for cracking the chicken-and-egg problem, then covers scaling, quality control, and regrets. Key finding: constrain by geography or category, focus on supply first, and use direct sales and word of mouth early.

principles.text: Start with the smallest viable marketplace: constrain by geography if service is physical, otherwise by category.
principles.quote: if the service requires physical interaction if you have to like pick up food or get in a car or stay at home that's it you can constraint it geographically

principles.text: Most marketplaces should focus on supply first; 80% of those studied did.
principles.quote: eighty percent of companies focused on supply so I take away there is most likely you're gonna want to focus on supply initially when you're building a marketplace

principles.text: Early supply growth is mostly unscalable direct sales, not SEO, viral loops or paid ads.
principles.quote: Dirk sales was the biggest lever by far across all these companies which surprised me I thought I was gonna be like forints marketing or SEO or viral loops and it turned out it's just sales

principles.text: Pick the few growth levers that work and double down; companies used only about two and a half levers on average.
principles.quote: even though there are many ways to grow supply probably there's going to be just a few that work for you and so learning there is don't try to do them all just pick the ones that seem to be working and double down on those

principles.text: Demand growth is led by word of mouth, which signals product-market fit; supply can also drive demand.
principles.quote: where to mouth is by far the biggest driver of growth for all of these companies which is really amazing and to me that just reaffirms how important product market fit is

principles.text: Don't expand into new business lines early; deepen the core and add new layers later once growth plateaus.
principles.quote: in the general case you don't want to do that because it's very hard to get any kind of business operating
